subject: Money
title: Purchasing Power
description: A micro-lesson that makes Purchasing Power usable.

hook.text: A dollar in 1970 had the purchasing power of $7.96 today. Your savings account is slowly evaporating.

buildup.text: Purchasing power is what your money can actually buy. Inflation erodes it silently, year after year.

discovery.text: If your salary rises 3% but inflation is 4%, you got a pay cut. Nominal gains can mask real losses.

twist.text: Cash under the mattress loses 2-3% annually. Saving money without investing it is guaranteed to lose value.

climax.text: Purchasing power is the real measure of wealth. What matters isn't how much you have but what it can buy.

punchline.text: A dollar saved is a dollar shrinking.

quiz.question: What happens if your salary rises 3% but inflation is 4%?
options: You effectively got a pay cut
